historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 12, Page 292-293. Wahhab ibn Abd al-Wahhab was born in 1703 in Uyainah, near the city of Dammam, in the eastern Arabian Peninsula. He initially focused on purifying the Islamic faith in Najd by eliminating the perceived influences of bid'ah (innovations) and shirk (associating partners with Allah). His movement gained significant support and spread throughout the Arabian Peninsula and the Arabian Gulf region during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Wahhabi movement in Najd, Arabia.

historical_references.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica. Wahhab, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab. Born 1703, Uyainah, near Dammam, Arabia. He is best known as the founder of the Wahhabi movement, a religious reformist movement that emerged in the Arabian Peninsula during the late 18th century. Wahhab's teachings emphasized a return to the fundamentals of Islam, rejecting the veneration of saints and the use of intercession in prayer. The movement gained widespread influence through military conquests and diplomacy, spreading throughout the Arabian Peninsula and the Gulf region.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Wahhabi movement, promoting a return to fundamental Islamic teachings.
